overview.title: Overview
overview.heroTitle: Bring responsive experiences closer to everyone.
overview.summary: Keep application teams focused on device, player, and member experiences—with a clear plan for growth, resilience, and ownership.
help: OCI NoSQL
Oracle NoSQL Database Cloud Service: managed tables for key-value, document, and typed data.
Table
Rows identified by a primary key. A JSON column can hold flexible document content.
Static showcase
Every example is synthetic. No cloud connection, telemetry, or resource change is made.

availability.title: Availability & scale
availability.pill: Grow with a deliberate capacity model
availability.heroTitle: Meet changing demand without managing servers.
availability.summary: Choose how to fund throughput and where data should live, while keeping application freshness and regional access requirements visible.
help: Read and Write Units
Throughput accounting depends on operation and data size; request count alone is not capacity.
On-demand
The service manages read/write capacity for the table. Service and storage limits still apply.
Global Active Table
A table replicated asynchronously between regions, with local reads and writes.
Dedicated hosted environment
Tenancy-dedicated capacity, requested through Oracle. Currently excludes Global Active Tables.

recovery.title: Data protection & disaster recovery
recovery.heroTitle: Keep a tested path back to service.
recovery.summary: Plan separately for a regional disruption and for unwanted data changes. The copy you rely on determines the recovery work your team must rehearse.
help: Regional redirection
The application moves to another configured regional endpoint. It is not a customer-controlled node promotion.
Recovery point
The data state available after recovery. No measured or guaranteed RPO is provided by this simulation.
Retained export
Customer-managed files and schema used as recovery input. Retention, capture consistency, and restore validation require a deliberate process.

migration.title: Migration & modernization
migration.heroTitle: Move application data with controlled cutover.
migration.summary: Choose a manageable migration boundary and prove the new application path before customers depend on it.
help: Migrator
A source-to-sink data movement utility. A data import is not proof of application compatibility.
Cutover
A customer-controlled change to application traffic and write ownership after validation.
Display-only samples
Commands are documentation examples. Executing them separately requires installation, IAM, reviewed configuration, and a demo target.

observability.title: Observability & operations
observability.eyebrow: From a service signal to a decision
observability.heroTitle: Turn table signals into practical action.
observability.summary: Connect customer symptoms to table demand and application behavior, then verify whether the chosen change helped.
help: oci_nosql
The OCI Monitoring namespace for service metrics. Preserve the time window, statistic, and table dimensions.
Throttle count
A count of throttling exceptions over a period; correlate with the application before diagnosing impact.
Replica lag
A receiver-side replication signal, expressed in milliseconds. It is neither a global consistency guarantee nor a measured RPO.
Missing samples
Unknown is not zero. Show No samples or Unavailable and investigate collection separately.

security.title: Security & governance
security.heroTitle: Give each application only needed access.
security.summary: Build an adoption boundary that teams can explain: who can use the data, how it is reached, and who owns its lifecycle.
help: IAM policy
Defines which principals may perform which actions on resources in a compartment.
Service endpoint
A regional access point; configure and validate the application network path. Do not assume a table has a Cache-style private endpoint.
CMEK
Customer-managed keys require a dedicated environment enabled for that feature and customer key lifecycle management.
Audit boundary
OCI Audit records supported API activity. It is not presented here as a complete row-read or application audit trail.

patterns.title: Workload patterns
patterns.pill: Follow the data behind the experience
patterns.heroTitle: Build around the moments users value.
patterns.summary: Explore small application stories that connect a data model to a customer outcome, with the ownership and tradeoffs in view.

regional.label: Regional disruption
regional.title: Keep another region ready to serve
regional.summary: Global Active Tables provide writable regional replicas. Your application needs a tested policy for choosing another region when its usual endpoint cannot be reached.

stages.title: Serve locally
stages.text: Both regional replicas can accept reads and writes. The illustrated application uses Region A.

stages.title: Detect disruption
stages.text: Region A is unreachable from this application. Retry and timeout handling belongs to the client; recent remote updates may not yet be visible in Region B.

stages.title: Redirect the application
stages.text: The customer routing policy selects the Region B endpoint. Region B is already writable; there is no customer-operated replica promotion.

stages.title: Validate and reconcile
stages.text: Check business operations and replication after connectivity returns. Investigate conflicting updates before returning traffic under your policy.

runbook: Prepare
Create eligible replicas and test regional access.
Detect
Correlate client errors and regional signals.
Redirect
Apply your application routing and retry policy.
Reconcile
Validate data freshness and recovered-region behavior.

export.label: Retained export
export.title: Recover from a deliberately retained copy
export.summary: A customer-managed Migrator export provides a separate recovery input. Decide when to capture it, where to retain it, and how to validate an import before an incident.

stages.title: Choose a capture boundary
stages.text: Coordinate source writes and the export scope. Do not assume an online export is a transactionally consistent snapshot.

stages.title: Export and retain
stages.text: Run the documented Migrator workflow. Protect the files and schema, record capture context, and check completion and error counts.

stages.title: Import separately
stages.text: Restore the selected files into an empty demo/recovery target using a reviewed schema and permissions. This writes rows and consumes capacity.

stages.title: Validate before routing
stages.text: Compare counts, keys, values, indexes, and expiry semantics. Only then decide whether to route application traffic to the recovery target.

runbook: Capture
Document source-write coordination and copy time.
Retain
Govern files, schema, access, and retention.
Restore
Import into an empty isolated target.
Validate
Check data and application behavior before cutover.

file.label: File import
file.title: Bring a reviewed data set into NoSQL
file.summary: Use supported JSON or CSV inputs with NoSQL Database Migrator. Rework keys and schema before import; an accepted file format does not establish application compatibility.

stages.title: Map the data
stages.text: Choose primary and shard keys; validate field types and required transformations.

stages.title: Prepare the target
stages.text: Prepare an empty target, scoped access, and capacity. Review configuration before running Migrator outside this showcase.

stages.title: Import the fixture
stages.text: The illustrative migration writes both input records without errors. No cloud operation is performed here.

stages.title: Check before cutover
stages.text: Verify keys, representative values, query behavior, expiry, and application access. Retain a rollback plan.

runbook: Map
Review keys, types, and transformations.
Prepare
Scope IAM and use an empty target.
Import
Reconcile written, skipped, and failed records.
Validate
Exercise application reads before cutover.

onprem.label: Oracle NoSQL source
onprem.title: Move existing NoSQL data deliberately
onprem.summary: Migrator can read an on-premises Oracle NoSQL source and write to the cloud service. Validate cloud constraints, access, and application configuration separately.

stages.title: Assess the source
stages.text: Inventory schemas, keys, queries, security, and expiry. Check the cloud target against your application requirements.

stages.title: Coordinate the copy
stages.text: Arrange network access and permissions. Define a source-write pause or an independently designed change reconciliation process.

stages.title: Transfer records
stages.text: Run and observe Migrator. Reconcile errors and counts; this demonstration does not claim continuous change capture.

stages.title: Validate and switch
stages.text: Test SDK authentication, regional endpoints, query behavior, and capacity before application cutover.

runbook: Assess
Inventory schemas and client assumptions.
Coordinate
Control concurrent source changes.
Transfer
Check errors and counts.
Switch
Validate the application and rollback conditions.

phased.label: Phased adoption
phased.title: Move one application boundary at a time
phased.summary: A customer-designed rollout can start with an isolated workload. Keep a single documented owner for each write path and define how discrepancies will be resolved.

stages.title: Select a boundary
stages.text: Choose an independently testable workload and define its source of truth.

stages.title: Exercise the new path
stages.text: Validate a synthetic or approved test data set. Compare application results before changing traffic.

stages.title: Shift selected traffic
stages.text: The application team controls traffic and write ownership. This is not a built-in NoSQL migration feature.

stages.title: Review rollback
stages.text: Reconcile any changed data before rollback; switching an endpoint alone does not reverse writes.

runbook: Scope
Select an isolated workload.
Validate
Compare representative application results.
Shift
Change routing and write ownership together.
Observe
Apply explicit rollback criteria.

ingest.title: Make device context available to applications
ingest.summary: An ingestion application validates each reading and writes it under a deliberate key. NoSQL stores the row; device identity and input validation belong to the application.
ingest.result: One illustrative event stored. Reusing a device-only key would overwrite its previous reading; include an event key when history matters.

expiry.title: Separate operational retention from archives
expiry.summary: Set a row lifetime for disposable readings. After expiration the row is no longer returned; a separate archival policy is needed if history must survive.
expiry.result: Expiry is a data-lifecycle choice, not a backup. This illustration makes no promise about physical deletion timing.

local.title: Load the context behind a player session
local.summary: Read a player document by key. Keep session authorization in the application and choose read consistency according to the business action.
local.result: A profile read does not authorize a purchase or establish a globally consistent wallet.

global.title: Make concurrent profile changes explicit
global.summary: Two regions update the same player row in this synthetic example. Regional replication resolves the conflict using the later write timestamp.
global.result: The earlier blue-theme update is superseded in this example. Design high-value state around the required correctness rules.

profile.title: Let profile details evolve with the product
profile.summary: Keep a stable identity key while storing optional profile attributes in JSON. Your application still validates fields and enforces visibility.
profile.result: Flexible JSON accommodates optional fields. It does not remove access checks or the need to design indexes for query paths.

regional.title: Serve a traveling member closer to home
regional.summary: A regional replica lets the application read and write near a member. A recent change made elsewhere may take time to appear.
regional.result: Application routing selects the endpoint. Global Active Tables do not automatically route a traveling user.
